item.research_question: How can the limited ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) be overcome to achieve ultra-ductility while maintaining high strength?
item.material_system: Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 (at%) eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases; industrial A357 casting aluminum alloy
item.processing_route: Two cycles of 30% cold rolling followed by annealing at 1200 °C for 20 mins with water quenching; for A357: two cycles of 15% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins followed by two cycles of 30% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins
item.test_conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; in situ tensile tests in FE-SEM; loading-unloading-reloading tests for back stress measurement
key_findings: The phase-selectively recrystallized (PSR) EHEA achieves a uniform elongation of ∼33% and an engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ∼2.2 GPa.
The PSR EHEA exhibits a fracture true strain of ∼30%, which is double that of the As-cast (AC) alloy (∼14%) and the fully recrystallized (FR) alloy (∼17%).
The fracture true stress of the PSR EHEA reaches ∼1850 MPa, significantly higher than the AC (∼1390 MPa) and FR (∼1460 MPa) alloys.
The microcrack density in the fractured PSR specimen is only one-third of that in the FR specimen, even under a twofold nominal strain.
The local von Mises strain in the FCC phase can be up to 6 times higher than that in the B2 phase during deformation.
A back stress of ∼900 MPa near failure was quantitatively measured in the PSR EHEA, accounting for its high strain hardening capacity.
A B2 → body-centered tetragonal (BCT) phase transformation was observed in the PSR EHEA during deformation, with the crystal structure expanding ∼6% along the (200) direction.
The PSR strategy increased the elongation of the A357 aluminum alloy from ∼8% to ∼23% and doubled its tensile strength to ∼400 MPa.
item.mechanism: Phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) eliminates weak boundaries (lamellar phase boundaries in AC and high-density grain boundaries in FR) by inducing complete recrystallization in the soft FCC phase while maintaining a skeletal, non-recrystallized B2 phase that undergoes only recovery. This microstructure prevents premature crack nucleation at weak interfaces, allowing both phases to contribute to strain hardening simultaneously through high-density dislocation multiplication and a strain-induced B2 to BCT phase transformation, thereby exhausting the alloy's strain hardening capacity before fracture.
item.limitations: The proposed model for calculating the suitable deformation level for PSR is semi-quantitative because it ignores information on microstructure and strain rate.
item.future_work: Further modifications to the theoretical model to include microstructure and strain rate information; direct characterization of PSR behaviors under different rolling amounts and subsequent annealing to overcome the complexity of acquiring parameter values.
quotes: The PSR EHEA with a well-tailored PSR microstructure doubles the fracture strain to ∼30%.
The PSR prevents premature failure and enhances ductility by eliminating the lamellar structures in the AC alloy while avoiding the high-density PBs of the B2 phase in the FR alloy.
